title: Transatlantic data governance & KMS binding review — EmberCap
summary: Customer wanted confirmation that EU customer data can be pinned to EU processing, review of KMS / BYOK options, subprocessors, and contractual language for cross-border fallbacks. SE covered technical limits around KV cache and model routing. Action items: send subprocessor inventory, SOC 2/ISO docs, proposed DPA language and schedule KMS handshake PoC.
topics: Redwood Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted fallback
action_items: Sofia Marquez: Share latest subprocessor inventory + redacted SOC2 report (by 2026-12-18)
Ethan Wu: Prepare KMS handshake PoC plan and timing (by 2026-12-22)
Laura Chen / Priya Singh: Provide EmberCap legal preferred DPA clauses and residency constraints (by 2026-12-21)
Tom Hale: Provide sample traffic profile and token rates for PoC (by 2026-12-20)
next_steps: Redwood to circulate subprocessor spreadsheet and SOC2 artifacts
Schedule 90-minute KMS integration technical deep dive (SE-led)
Agree on acceptance criteria for region pinning PoC and rollback behavior
Legal teams to align on DPA language around cross-border fallbacks
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 14:00 UTC — Duration 58 mins — Recording available
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood CSM); Laura (EmberCap Head of Security), Marcus (EmberCap CTO), Priya (Legal), Tom (Infra)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, appreciate you making time, we'll do a quick agenda — region pinning, KMS/BYOK, subprocessors and contract questions.
[00:12] Laura: Great, thanks. High level — EmberCap needs to guarantee EU customer PHI stays in EU for processing and storage. Also want to know what happens if the model route falls back to US during spikes.
[00:28] Ethan: Yeah absolutely, so short answer we offer region pinning at the tenant level on Redwood Private and we can approximate on Dedicated with strong affinity rules. Hosted has region preferences but not hard locks unless we do a private deployment.
[00:45] Marcus: When you say "approximate" on Dedicated, what does that mean operationally? Could a token ever be routed to US infra?
[00:53] Ethan: Good question. Dedicated uses strong routing rules — primary affinity to EU pools. We only route cross‑border if the EU pool is saturated and policy allows a fallback, otherwise request is queued. For strict legal requirements we recommend Redwood Private or on‑prem.
[01:10] Priya: For regulatory purposes we need contractual guarantees. Can that be in the DPA that you will not process in non‑EU regions except under explicit written permission and emergency fallbacks with notice?
[01:24] Sofia: We can include that clause; our standard DPA has fallbacks for capacity and disaster recovery with notice periods. We should follow up with legal to put the exact language.
[01:34] Tom: Tech question — how do you handle encryption keys? We want BYOK and split keys if possible.
[01:40] Ethan: We support customer‑managed KMS for Redwood Private and Dedicated in many regions. BYOK for hosted is a bit more constrained today, we're working on KMS escrow and split key flows. For the PoC we can do a KMS handshake — customer KMS in EU, Redwood service accesses via short‑lived keys and we do zero‑knowledge logs.
[02:02] Laura: The handshake — does Redwood ever hold plaintext keys or escrowed keys? We need to guarantee HSM never gives a raw key copy.
[02:10] Ethan: We never persist your raw secret. The KMS flow uses grant tokens and ephemeral credentials. If we need escrowed material for disaster recovery, that's done via an audited HSM escrow vendor with contract controls — we can share the list.
[02:26] Marcus: What about KV cache — if a live session has prefixes cached, could that be replicated to a US instance?
[02:33] Ethan: KV cache is sharded to the serving pool local to the region. In fallback, we can either reject the request or replicate the cached state to a compatible pool; replication is controlled by policy. For strict residency we'd set replication to "no cross‑region replication" and rather throttle or fail, depending on SLA choices.
[02:55] Laura: Audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for access, key use, and model inferences. Retention 7 years for regulated customers. Can you export to our SIEM?
[03:08] Olivia: Yes, Redwood Console exposes audit logs, and we support push to customer SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export to a customer bucket. Retention can be configured; for Private we can align retention and export to your own storage in EU.
[03:23] Priya: Subprocessors — we need a full inventory and committed notice period before adding any new subprocessors. Also we require certain vendors to be excluded or to have contract parity.
[03:35] Sofia: We'll send the current subprocessor spreadsheet. We have most infra partners listed — cloud providers, monitoring, HSM vendor for escrow, and telemetry vendors. We do a 30‑day notice for major subprocessor changes in our enterprise contracts.
[03:49] Tom: If the customer bucket for logs is in EU S3, does Redwood ever pull logs into US for processing?
[03:57] Ethan: No, for Private and Dedicated we can ensure logs stay in the designated bucket and we don't pull them. For hosted customers, telemetry we collect is aggregated and can be processed in region‑hierarchies unless you specify residency requirements.
[04:14] Laura: Can you walk through an incident scenario — say EU pool fails and auto‑failover sends traffic to US for 30 minutes. What are the controls, and can we require consent before such a failover?
[04:27] Ethan: We support policies: auto‑failover with immediate routing, or manual approval for failover. For strict compliance you can select manual approval; in DR you'd give a breakglass policy with audit trail. We can add an audit hook that notifies security and requires two approvers.
[04:46] Sofia: Quick note — many customers pick Dedicated with burst capacity and a private control plane as the middle ground. It's a good tradeoff if you want predictable throughput and strong residency but still want Redwood to manage orchestration.
[04:58] Marcus: Latency tradeoffs — if we pin to EU only we expect higher costs due to insufficient batching across regions?
[05:05] Ethan: There's a small unit cost impact when you constraint regional placement because you lose global batching efficiency, but it's usually minor compared to data sovereignty needs. We'll model it in the PoC with your traffic profile.
[05:18] Priya: Contract questions — we need to add: specific DPA clause, notice periods, subprocessor veto list, key custody details and audit rights. Also SOC2 and ISO27001 evidence.
[05:30] Sofia: Understood — action: we'll share SOC2 & ISO docs and our standard DPA track changes.
[05:36] Laura: Can we get a redacted SOC2 Type II and the ISO cert? Also, any third‑party penetration test results?
[05:43] Olivia: Yes, we'll share redacted reports. For pentests we can share executive summaries.
[05:48] Marcus: For the PoC — timeline suggestion: 2 weeks to exchange docs, 1 week to scope, 2 weeks for KMS handshake PoC, then evaluation. Roughly 6 weeks.
[05:58] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. We'll follow up with calendar invites.

[END]
